cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 answers T2: westerlies would carry cold air without ocean storage.
cells.limitation: Philosopher turns T3, T6, T9 ignore the physical exchange around them.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T4 adds heat storage versus transport; T10 reuses that split.
cells.limitation: T7 to T9 add no new physical distinction; T8 only restates T5.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T1 versus T2 frames ocean current against westerlies.
cells.limitation: Nobody raises west versus east coast, Labrador Current or the Rockies.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T5 grants ocean storage while keeping atmospheric distribution.
cells.limitation: Section D settles on 'both' without showing how they combine.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D states storage plus transport as joint cause.
cells.limitation: T10 ends on which factor the user values, not a sharper question.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T5 accurately restates T4's storage claim before qualifying it.
cells.limitation: T8 claims T7's map suggestion ignores winds; T7 never said so.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T4 names the hidden premise: winds carry cold air absent ocean heat.
cells.limitation: T8 objection about seasonal wind variance is vague and unanswered.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T2 correctly names prevailing westerlies carrying maritime air inland.
cells.limitation: T1 'primary reason' is contested; T3 Russell quotation suspected inexact.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: Section E admits relative contribution of each remains unknown.
cells.limitation: T1 states the current as primary flatly; T3 guesses a fear.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T5 concedes the ocean stores heat.
cells.limitation: T9 reversal names no cause; Oceanographer never revises the primacy claim.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A names the ocean versus atmosphere question.
cells.limitation: T10 and Section E recast explanation as a preference between factors.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: Section A restates northern Europe versus Canada comparison.
cells.limitation: The phrase 'parts of Canada' never shapes any argument.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T7 offers a concrete thing to look at.
cells.limitation: T6 imposes simplicity versus completeness the user never stated.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T5 notes the inland reach as what the current misses.
cells.limitation: T3 invents a user fear about latitude labels.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on whether relative contribution is known.
cells.limitation: Which Canadian region (BC versus Labrador) is never asked or branched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T6 suggests the user may want both simple and complete answers.
cells.limitation: T3 asserts a fear; no alternative motives offered with a question.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3 surfaces latitude as a misleading guide to climate.
cells.limitation: Single-cause assumption only named in Section D, never examined in turns.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T6 contrasts simplicity with completeness.
cells.limitation: The contrast in T6 is artificial for an explanatory question.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T3 names a possible fear about latitude labels.
cells.limitation: T3 imputes fear with no basis in the question.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section D offers single-cause desire as possible oversimplification.
cells.limitation: T10 hands the user a value choice rather than a testable distinction.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: T1 and T2 define ocean transport and westerly circulation explanations.
cells.limitation: Topography and coast-side explanations never defined as candidates.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T8 says map-only reading costs the atmospheric interaction.
cells.limitation: Neither explanation's evidential cost or gap is spelled out.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E suggests comparing SST data with inland winds.
cells.limitation: Section E conditions on user preference, not an observable deciding fact.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section E flags the unknown relative contribution.
cells.limitation: Consequential unknowns not separated from minor ones anywhere.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: T7: look at January sea surface temperature maps.
cells.limitation: T7 step does not say what result would favour which explanation.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T2 plainly explains westerlies carrying moderated air inland.
cells.limitation: T6 and T8 use vague phrases like 'seasonal wind variance'.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T4 clearly targets T2's westerlies claim.
cells.limitation: T6 'both' and T9 'my focus' are loosely anchored.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Ten short turns read quickly.
cells.limitation: Three turns fall under 25 words per deterministic checks.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Titles mark ocean, atmosphere and philosophy positions distinctly.
cells.limitation: All three share one flat register; Philosopher hedges in T3, T6.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns are brief with little recap.
cells.limitation: Section E repeats T10's preference framing nearly verbatim.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T4 versus T5 contests which is the fundamental source.
cells.limitation: No vivid stake, such as a city comparison, makes the puzzle bite.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T9 Philosopher announces a shift in focus.
cells.limitation: T9 reversal names no earlier argument as cause.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T4 has a terse, confident edge.
cells.limitation: Minds sound like textbook summaries; no character in any turn.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T1 'massive heat conveyor' image.
cells.limitation: No analogy, concrete city or striking line anywhere.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T4 to T5 builds brief back-and-forth.
cells.limitation: Uniform rhythm throughout; T10 ends flat on an open preference.

strengths: T4 answers T2 by naming the premise that winds alone would carry cold air.
T1 and T2 define two competing mechanisms clearly at the outset.
T7 offers a concrete, specific thing to look at: January SST maps.
weaknesses: T10 and Section E turn an explanation into a preference over which factor the user values.
Nobody raises the west versus east coast comparison, Labrador Current or Rockies.
Philosopher's T3 imputes a fear and T9 reverses with no stated cause.

symptoms.observed: Ends on user preference instead of an observable fact separating explanations.
symptoms.evidence: depends on whether you value heat storage or heat transport more

symptoms.observed: Never compares Canada's coasts or names the cold Labrador Current.
symptoms.evidence: the current alone does not explain the inland reach

symptoms.observed: Asserts a user fear with no alternative motive or question.
symptoms.evidence: Maybe you fear that the simple latitude label is a false guide

symptoms.observed: Philosopher changes focus without naming what argument caused it.
symptoms.evidence: I drop my focus on categorization and now emphasize

symptoms.observed: Never asks or branches on which Canadian region the user means.
symptoms.evidence: brings warm water from the tropics to the northern Atlantic

findings.description: Three turns fall under 25 words per deterministic checks.
Quoted phrase attributed to Russell's Problems of Philosophy may be inexact or not from that book.
North Atlantic Drift as the primary reason is contested; atmospheric stationary waves and coast-side effects are argued to dominate.
Attributes a fear to the user with no basis in the question.

rubric_fit_notes: Criterion 4 fits a purely physical explanatory question loosely; ratings reflect the debate's thin and partly invented motive claims rather than a missing life reflection. My judgment on T1 accuracy relies on memory of climate literature and is reported as suspected.
question_type_note: Read as exploratory: C5 judged on whether an observable fact would separate ocean from atmospheric explanations, and the preference-based ending was deducted in C3.1 and C5.3.
